summary: US-002: Create and publish a GA event
description:
**As** an organizer, **I want** to create a venue, event, performance and GA ticket type via the catalog API and see it listed on the storefront.

**Priority:** P0
**Depends on:** US-001 (TKT-25)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Catalog API: create venue (GA capacity), event, dated performance, ticket type with EUR price; persisted; OpenAPI contract published
- [ ] Publishing a performance emits a domain event; storefront lists published performances with name/date/price (browser-verified)
- [ ] Public catalog reads (event list, event detail) carry explicit Cache-Control TTLs per ADR-004 tiers; the storefront page issues one aggregated call and does not re-fetch within the TTL
- [ ] Entities carry an organizer_id even though v1 has one organizer

Quality gates: `make check` green (defined in US-001, mirrors CI); contract tests for touched service boundaries; UI: browser-verified with screenshot in PR; money paths: NF525 journal chain verifies (from US-004).

binding.rule: We adopt Go for all backend services and TypeScript + React for the three frontends (storefront, back office, scanner). Money is represented as integer minor units + ISO currency code everywhere; floats are banned on money paths.

We build five Go services (catalog, inventory, commerce, payments, access) behind an API gateway, with an event bus for the domain event stream; every entity carries a tenant/organizer id from day one. Docker Compose only.

Every public read endpoint declares a volatility-tiered TTL with explicit Cache-Control (seat maps: hours; event lists/detail: minutes; price display: ~1 min; availability: seconds; hold/order/scan state: never cached); hot events are served from in-memory structures refreshed/invalidated from the write path; frontends make few aggregated calls (one per page view, not per widget) and refresh on the endpoint's TTL cadence; writes are never cached.
